rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials in iterations 1 to 3 ended off_track with zero completions. Max error sits at about 0.061 m, the off-track limit max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), so each run ends after one excursion on a bend. RMS error is stuck near 0.022 to 0.030, and steering oscillation is low (0.06 to 0.29), so this is not jitter or instability. Progress is 0.04 to 0.48, and the best oval progress came at ki 0.4 (iteration 2). Raising ki to 0.8 and dropping speed to 1.0 (iteration 3) cut oval progress from 0.48 to 0.40 while helping s-bend slightly, so the integral and speed changes are not the main lever. Hypothesis H2 from iteration 2 is now the leading one: the outer sensors at x = ±0.03 m with a 12 mm footprint lose the 25 mm tape on sharp bends. The signal then collapses toward zero, and the robot drifts wide before the correction is strong enough. Changes this iteration: (1) widen the sensor spread to x = ±0.045 m, so the outer sensors see the tape earlier on a bend, and enlarge sensor_size to 16 mm so each footprint keeps a larger share of the tape as the robot turns. (2) Reduce wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, which raises turn rate for the same PWM differential and gives more steering authority on tight bends. (3) Reduce mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia. (4) Set ki to 0.6 (between the best value and the iteration 3 value) and keep kp 3.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.0. Speed is held at 1.0 so this iteration isolates the geometry change. body_width stays at 0.12. Expected result: max_error falls below 0.06 on s-bend and slalom, and progress rises above 0.3 on all tracks. Completion inside 3 s is still unlikely; survival is the priority. Hypotheses: (H1) with wider sensors, progress rises on the sharp tracks without raising line_loss_events. (H2) if progress stays near 0.1 on slalom, the limiting factor is the controller response to direction changes, so the next step is a higher kd or lower kp. Measurements wanted: progress and max_error per track, where max_error occurs, line_loss_events, and whether steering_oscillation rises with the narrower wheel track.
